topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by connecting histopathology practical observations to cellular transformation and outlining the learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Tumor Virology and the Discovery of Cellular Oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the historical investigation of infectious tumor viruses and how retroviral gene capture demonstrated that cancer originates from altered normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental Assays for Cellular Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the phenotypic hallmarks and laboratory culture and animal assays used to test whether specific genes or mutations can transform cells.

topics.label: Classification and Mechanisms of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define oncogenes, tumor suppressor genes, and mutation types, illustrating their functional impact through cell cycle checkpoint regulation and allelic mechanisms such as dominant-negative p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Consequences of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the distinctions between sequence and chromosomal instability, detailing the specific DNA repair failures, replication errors, and mitotic defects that produce them.

topics.label: Multistep Mutational Progression in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the Vogelstein model of colorectal cancer to illustrate how the stepwise accumulation and ordering of mutations drive tumor development.

topics.label: Hereditary Cancer Predisposition Syndromes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how inheriting a single mutated allele in gatekeeper or caretaker genes accelerates cancer onset across clinical syndromes such as Lynch syndrome, FAP, and hereditary breast cancer.
